newsitem.title: UK: Gold weakens to key $350 level, then comes off lows.
newsitem.headline: Gold weakens to key $350 level, then comes off lows.

text.p: A beleagured gold market sank below the psychological $350 an ounce level on Wednesday, the lowest price in more than three years, but a midday bounce then lifted it off the lows.
Battered by a surging dollar and stock markets, and under pressure from fresh selling, gold traded as low as $349.65/$349.95 an ounce in early business, dealers said.
But values crept up from the lows to fix at $351.20 an ounce in the afternoon, compared to the morning fixing of $350.10, the lowest since September 15, 1993.
"New York looked nervous coming in, but prices managed a little bounce," a dealer said. Wall Street meanwhile suffered a steep slide and the dollar retreated from early gains.
"There is huge interest at this level with over-the-counter options expiring at the end of the month," he added, noting that prices may range between $348 and $352 for the time being.
But eventually, dealers and analysts said, prices were likely to resume heading lower, with the nearest support level pegged at $345 an ounce.
"That is quite a good retracement level and the intersection of a long-term trend," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Gold may even test the waters at $330, the significant low level from 1993, some analysts said.
Prices have been sliding steadily lower to levels not seen for more than three years since hitting a high of $417 an ounce in February 1996.
Investors have ignored gold in favour of strong equities markets, while physical buyers have sat back waiting for prices to bottom out.

Meanwhile, market sentiment has become increasingly bearish as fears grow that European central banks will sell their gold reserves ahead of European Monetary Union to raise money to meet treaty financial criteria.
Tuesday's upbeat remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan spelled more bad news for bullion as the dollar soared against the mark and yen, further encouraging holders of gold to sell.
The other precious metals eased, then perked up in sympathy with gold.
Silver, shadowing gold in a subdued fashion, was off lows but down one cent from Tuesday's London close, at $4.71/$4.73.
Platinum, like gold trading at 3-1/4 year lows, was down $1.75 $356.00/$357.00. Its sister metal palladium was little changed at $120.75/$121.75.
